name: Nyan Cat
blurb: A pixel cat with a Pop-Tart body flying through space on a rainbow, to a looping song
title: Nyan Cat Meme: Meaning, Origin & the Song
description: Nyan Cat is a pixel-art GIF of a Pop-Tart cat trailing a rainbow, drawn by Chris Torres in April 2011 and set to a Japanese "nyan" song on YouTube days later.
answer: Nyan Cat is an 8-bit style animation of a grey cat with a pink, sprinkled Pop-Tart for a body, flying through space and leaving a rainbow behind it, set to an endlessly looping song that repeats "nyan" (Japanese for "meow"). The artist Chris Torres (prguitarman) posted the GIF on 2 April 2011, and on 5 April a YouTube user paired it with a Japanese song, "Nyanyanyanyanyanyanya!". The video was one of the most-watched YouTube videos of 2011 and won a Webby Award in 2012.

body: A small pixelated cat with a grey head, legs and tail and a pink, sprinkled Pop-Tart for a body paddles its legs as it flies through a dark starry sky. Behind it trails a striped rainbow that wiggles to the beat.
The music is just as important: a cheerful chiptune-style tune with a high voice singing "nya" over and over. The loop is so catchy that people famously left it running for hours.

head: Date
Event
rows: The producer daniwell uploads "Nyanyanyanyanyanyanya!", sung by the Vocaloid Hatsune Miku, to Niconico.
A cover using the UTAU voice Momone Momo is uploaded; this is the version later heard in Nyan Cat.
Chris Torres posts the Pop-Tart cat GIF on 2 April; on 5 April YouTube user saraj00n combines it with the song as "Nyan Cat".
The video becomes the fifth most-viewed YouTube video of the year.
Nyan Cat wins the Webby Award for Meme of the Year; the song appears in the game Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA F.
Torres and the creator of Keyboard Cat sue over their characters' use in the Scribblenauts games; the case is settled in September.

body: Torres based the drawing on his own cat, Marty, who died in November 2012.

ul: Long loops: remixes and extended versions several hours long, and people timing how long they can listen.
Remixes in other styles and national "versions" with different flags and food bodies.
Progress bars, cursors and game skins in the Nyan Cat design.
A shorthand for pure, cheerful early-2010s internet nonsense.

body: Nyan Cat is a classic of the early-2010s YouTube era and is still instantly recognisable. Its creator owns the character and has defended it legally, which is why official products carry his name. The original upload moved to a dedicated Nyan Cat channel in November 2023, after passing 200 million views.

faq.a: Chris Torres, an artist from Dallas, Texas, known online as prguitarman, who posted the animation in April 2011. The song comes from the Japanese producer daniwell.
It is the Japanese sound a cat makes, like "meow" in English.

faq.q: Why does Nyan Cat have a Pop-Tart body?
faq.a: During a livestreamed charity drawing session, two viewers suggested "Pop-Tart" and "cat", and Torres drew a mix of both. He later animated it into the GIF.
